audit_findings.title: The anchor and perimeter do not describe a stable combined-company claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 included only $1,078.7 million of post-close IPG revenue and a $153.1 million IPG net loss; planned disposals had approximately $3.2 billion of prior-year revenue, while 2026 first-half disposals and held-for-sale businesses contributed $1,194.7 million of revenue and $86.4 million of EBITA
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE reflects roughly one month of IPG, the share denominator reflects post-merger ownership, and pending disposals change future OE and the bridge perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, in connection with the Merger we identified planned dispositions of certain businesses in 2026 that we expect will occur within the next twelve months (see Note 14 to the consolidated financial statements).
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, not hypothetical. The 2025 anchor does not represent a full year of the businesses supporting the post-merger shares, while dispositions continue to remove earnings and assets. Missing full-year IPG earnings tends to understate value, but earnings removed through dispositions and related proceeds or liabilities could move value either way. The filed amounts are large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using a parent-attributable full post-merger period and reconcile each completed or pending disposal's OE, proceeds, transferred liabilities, and share count to one consistent perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Full-year cost of the acquired debt is absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $210 million expected annual increase in net interest expense, equal to 142.1% of the $147.8 million anchor; 2026 first-half interest expense increased by $120.5 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: Because interest remains inside equity-level OE, mechanically growing the 2025 anchor omits most of the post-merger interest burden.
audit_findings.evidence: Going forward we expect net interest expense to increase by $210 million, primarily from assumed IPG debt and refinancing activities during the year.
audit_findings.explanation: The model's omission is demonstrated: it contains no explicit adjustment from the partial-year anchor to full-year acquired-debt interest. The disclosed $210 million annual burden exceeds the entire anchor and is therefore capable of materially changing forecast OE. This finding addresses the omitted cost only; the simultaneously omitted full-year IPG operating earnings belong in the separate perimeter reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Recompute OE from a full combined-company period using actual interest expense and refinancing rates, matched to the same period's IPG operating earnings, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may permanently capitalize merger-period one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 identified items reduced operating income by $2,141.4 million and parent net income by $1,750.5 million, 11.8 times the $147.8 million anchor; 2026 first-half identified items reduced parent net income by another $150.9 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Including nonrecurring charges in anchor OE understates normalized OE, while excluding recurring integration or restructuring cash costs would overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The net impact of these items reduced operating income for 2025 by $2,141.4 million ($1,750.5 million after-tax) and reduced diluted net income per share - Omnicom Group Inc. by $8.50.
audit_findings.explanation: The dominance of merger-period charges is demonstrated, but the amount improperly included in or excluded from the $147.8 million OE calculation is unresolved without its reconciliation. The known after-tax 2025 charges vastly exceed the anchor, and additional costs continued in 2026, so classification could materially change value in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Produce a line-by-line OE reconciliation separating cash paid, accrued cash obligations, noncash impairments, recurring restructuring, transaction expenses, and disposition effects; rerun with only economically supportable normalization adjustments.

audit_findings.title: The bridge assumes all cash is surplus despite operating-liquidity demands
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified required operating cash; the full $3,336.2 million bridge addition equals $11.31 per share and 61.6% of the $5,413.0 million base equity value, while 2026 first-half operating-capital use was $2,434.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for client obligations, seasonal working capital, pooling arrangements, or repatriation cannot be added as surplus in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Working capital, which we define as current assets minus current liabilities, is our principal non-discretionary funding requirement.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding every dollar of cash as surplus is demonstrated, but the distributable portion is not. The exposure is material because cash supplies most of the modeled base equity value, and the filed working-capital use shows substantial liquidity demands. The exact overstatement remains unquantified until minimum operating cash is established.
audit_findings.action: Determine parent-accessible excess cash after client-funded balances, seasonal working-capital needs, notional-pool requirements, foreign taxes, and restrictions, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: NCI basis and redeemable NCI claims are not reconciled
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified basis correction; latest filed redeemable NCI was $318.8 million and ordinary NCI was $610.4 million, totaling $929.2 million or $3.15 per share and 17.2% of base equity value; 2025 NCI income was $98.2 million versus the $147.8 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with consolidated cash-flow adjustments and cash, while ordinary and redeemable NCI claims are not consistently allocated or deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: Assuming that the subsidiaries perform at their current and projected profit levels, at December 31, 2025, the aggregate estimated amount we could be required to pay in future periods is $ 363.2 million, of which $ 164.5 million is currently exercisable by the holders.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed parent/consolidated basis is a demonstrated methodological error. The exact correction is unresolved because the record does not allocate D&A, capex, working capital, and cash to NCI, and ordinary NCI book value is not necessarily its fair-value claim. Nevertheless, the filed NCI balances and income are large relative to modeled equity value and anchor OE, making a material overstatement reasonably possible.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE and the bridge entirely on a parent-attributable basis, or use consolidated OE and explicitly value and deduct ordinary and redeemable NCI while retaining the associated earnings consistently.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is an omitted non-debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $244.8 million, equal to $0.83 per share and 4.5% of the $5,413.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Financing-classified earn-out payments may bypass operating-cash-flow-derived OE and therefore require a bridge deduction unless their economic cost is already captured.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, contingent purchase price liabilities were $ 214.9 million and $ 220.1 million, respectively, of which $ 95.8 million and $ 56.0 million, respectively, were classified as current liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed liability is omitted from the bridge. Deducting the entire $244.8 million would reduce base value from $18.34 to approximately $17.51 per share, still about 78.8% below the $82.62 market price. It therefore does not change the present valuation conclusion, although it should be corrected for completeness.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the settlement obligation at the valuation date and rerun the bridge with a $244.8 million deduction unless a documented OE reconciliation proves the full economic cost is already included without double counting.
